title: Nonnegativity of the switching failure indicator
statement: Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$, let $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and fix signs on the coordinates outside $J$. Form the restricted function by varying the signs on $J$ while keeping those outside signs fixed, and let its decision-tree depth be the least depth of a binary decision tree computing the corresponding function on $\{0,1\}^n$. The indicator that this depth is at least $k$ is nonnegative.
hypotheses_covered: $J$ is a subset of the $n$ coordinates
A fixed sign assignment on coordinates outside $J$
